claim: To stay backward compatible with AWS Glue, Lake Formation starts with the Super permission granted to the IAMAllowedPrincipals group on all existing Data Catalog resources and with Use only IAM access control enabled for new resources. Access is then controlled solely by IAM policies and individual Lake Formation permissions are not in effect.
question: What are the initial default security settings of Lake Formation?

values.display: The Super permission is granted to the group IAMAllowedPrincipals
Use only IAM access control

qualifiers.condition: change the default settings and upgrade existing resources to use Lake Formation permissions

evidence.quote: The Super permission is granted to the group IAMAllowedPrincipals on all existing AWS Glue Data Catalog resources.
"Use only IAM access control" settings are enabled for new Data Catalog resources.

These settings effectively cause access to Data Catalog resources and Amazon S3 locations to be controlled solely by AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies. Individual Lake Formation permissions are not in effect.

claim: The IAMAllowedPrincipals group includes any IAM users and roles allowed access to Data Catalog resources by your IAM policies. The Super permission lets a principal perform every supported Lake Formation operation on the database or table where it is granted.
question: What do IAMAllowedPrincipals and the Super permission mean in Lake Formation?

values.display: includes any IAM users and roles that are allowed access to your Data Catalog resources
perform every supported Lake Formation operation on the database or table

evidence.quote: The IAMAllowedPrincipals group includes any IAM users and roles that are allowed access to your Data Catalog resources by your IAM policies. The Super permission enables a principal to perform every supported Lake Formation operation on the database or table on which it is granted.

claim: To have Lake Formation permissions manage access to Data Catalog databases and tables, change the default security settings for new resources and also change the settings for existing Data Catalog resources.
question: What two changes move a Data Catalog from IAM-only control to Lake Formation permissions?

values.display: Change the default security settings for new resources
Change the settings for existing Data Catalog resources

evidence.quote: Change the default security settings for new resources.
Change the settings for existing Data Catalog resources.

claim: With the PutDataLakeSettings API you can make Lake Formation enforce metadata and data access control on new databases and tables, which revokes all Lake Formation permissions from IAMAllowedPrincipals on them, or enforce control only by IAM, which grants Super to IAMAllowedPrincipals. You can override this when you create a database.
question: How do you change the default permission model for new databases and tables?

values.display: revokes all Lake Formation permissions from the IAMAllowedPrincipals group on new databases and tables
grants the Super Lake Formation permission to the IAMAllowedPrincipals group on new databases and tables

qualifiers.condition: you can override the setting when you create a database

evidence.quote: This action effectively revokes all Lake Formation permissions from the IAMAllowedPrincipals group on new databases and tables. When you create a database, you can override this setting.
This grants the Super Lake Formation permission to the IAMAllowedPrincipals group on new databases and tables. When you create a database, you can override this setting.

claim: To add S3 storage to your data lake you register the location with Lake Formation. You can then use Lake Formation permissions for fine-grained access control to Data Catalog objects that point to the location and to the underlying data there.
question: What does registering an S3 location with Lake Formation do?

values.display: you register the location (Data lake location) with AWS Lake Formation
fine-grained access control to AWS Glue Data Catalog objects

evidence.quote: To add a data location as storage in your data lake, you register the location (Data lake location) with AWS Lake Formation. You can then use Lake Formation permissions for fine-grained access control to AWS Glue Data Catalog objects that point to this location and to the underlying data in the location.

claim: When you register an S3 location, that path and all folders under it are registered. Locations are buckets or prefixes under a bucket, not individual objects.

buckets or prefixes under a bucket, but not individual Amazon S3 objects

claim: Lake Formation permissions are recommended for structured data arranged in tables with rows and columns. For object-based unstructured data, consider Amazon S3 Access Grants to manage data access.

consider using Amazon S3 access grants to manage data access

evidence.quote: Lake Formation permissions are recommended for structured data (arranged in tables with rows and columns). If your data contains object-based unstructured data, consider using Amazon S3 access grants to manage data access.

claim: When registering a location, the default IAM role is the AWSServiceRoleForLakeFormationDataAccess service-linked role, or you can choose a custom role. You can update a registered location only if it was registered with a custom role; otherwise you deregister and register it again.
question: Which role does Lake Formation use by default to register a location, and can you edit it?

values.display: AWSServiceRoleForLakeFormationDataAccess service-linked role (the default)
update a registered location or other details only when you register it using a custom IAM role

qualifiers.condition: service-linked role locations cannot be edited

evidence.quote: For IAM role, choose either the AWSServiceRoleForLakeFormationDataAccess service-linked role (the default) or a custom IAM role that meets the requirements in Requirements for roles used to register locations.

You can update a registered location or other details only when you register it using a custom IAM role. To edit a location registered using a service-linked role, you should deregister the location and register it again.

claim: A principal does not need data location permissions to read or write the underlying data; SELECT or INSERT data access permissions are sufficient. Data location permissions apply only to creating Data Catalog resources that point to the location, and they cover all child locations.
question: Do you need data location permissions to query a table in a registered location?

values.display: does not need data location permissions to perform read/write operations
has data location permissions on all child locations

evidence.quote: A principal does not need data location permissions to perform read/write operations on the underlying data. It is sufficient to have the SELECT or INSERT data access permissions. Data location permissions apply only to creating Data Catalog resources that point to the location.
If a principal is granted data location permissions on a location, the principal has data location permissions on all child locations.
